transcript.text:
Lincoln! I've been riding for a week handling depositions in Bloomington, trusting you to mind the office, and I come back to this! The Henderson deposition is gone — I cannot find it anywhere on your desk or mine. Judge Davis's letter has been sitting here unopened for five days! You told me you'd keep things in order while I was away!

*throws hat down on desk and gestures wildly at the cluttered papers*

How am I supposed to run a respectable law practice when I can't even trust my own partner to maintain the most basic order? Do you have any idea how this looks? Henderson's case goes to trial next week!

Let us work together to rectify this situation. I will assist you in locating the Henderson deposition and ensure that Judge Davis's letter is promptly attended to. We must prioritize getting everything back in order to uphold the reputation of our law practice.

Please forgive my oversight, William. I value our partnership and will make it a priority to maintain better organization in the future. Let us address these issues together so that we can move forward effectively.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*paces back and forth, still visibly agitated*

"Assist me in locating it?" Lincoln, that deposition didn't sprout legs and walk away on its own! It was right there on my desk when I left — I specifically told you where it was and that it needed to be filed safely!

*runs hand through hair in exasperation*

And this isn't the first time, is it? How many times have I come back to find important documents buried under your newspapers and poetry books? You sit here reading your Euclid and your Shakespeare while clients' cases hang in the balance!

*picks up Judge Davis's unopened letter and waves it*

Five days, Lincoln! Judge Davis is one of our most important contacts on the circuit. What if this was time-sensitive? What if he needed a response for a case?

I appreciate your apology, but I need more than words — I need action! I need to know that when I leave this office, the practice we've built together won't fall into chaos. Do you understand the gravity of this? Henderson is counting on us, and right now I don't even know where to begin looking for that deposition!

*takes a breath, trying to calm himself slightly*

Now, think carefully — when did you last see that Henderson deposition? Where exactly might you have put it?

*stops and faces him directly, voice rising*

Or when Mrs. Patterson came in for her appointment and you'd completely forgotten because you were down at the courthouse listening to some debate?

*voice cracking slightly with frustration*

I work myself to exhaustion trying to build something here, Lincoln. I ride circuit, I handle the depositions, I keep the books, I maintain correspondence — and I need a partner, not a... a philosopher who happens to occasionally practice law!

*opens Judge Davis's letter and scans it quickly*

Now help me search. Check your coat pockets, check under that pile of newspapers, check everywhere. And while we're searching, you can tell me exactly what you DID do while I was gone for an entire week!

I don't want to be at odds with you. You're brilliant in court when you apply yourself, and clients trust you. But I can't keep running this office alone while you... while you what? Dream about higher callings?

*sets the deposition down carefully on the cleared corner of his own desk, then turns back to Lincoln with a weary expression*

Lincoln, I... 

*takes a deep breath, some of the anger draining away into exhaustion*

I believe you're sorry. I do. But that's the trouble, isn't it? You're always sorry. You're always contrite and you always promise to do better, and yet...

*gestures around the office*

Look, I know you have a brilliant legal mind. When you focus on a case, when you truly engage, you can sway a jury like no one I've ever seen. Your arguments before the Supreme Court in the Rock Island Bridge case were masterful. But those moments of brilliance don't sustain a practice, Lincoln. The daily grind does. The careful attention to detail does.

*sits on the edge of his desk, rubbing his temples*

And I see you staring out that window sometimes, reading about the Kansas-Nebraska Act, following Douglas's speeches. I'm not blind. I know your mind is elsewhere — on bigger things than property disputes and contract law.

*looks up at him directly*

So I have to ask you plainly, as your friend and partner: Are you still committed to this practice? To THIS work? Or are we just... are we just going through the motions until something else calls you away?

transcript.text:

transcript.text:
*stands up from the desk, studying Lincoln's face intently*

You say you're committed, and yet in the same breath you admit your mind wanders to "larger questions of justice and equality." Lincoln, those aren't just idle daydreams for you anymore, are they? I see the letters you've been receiving from political contacts. I hear the talk around Springfield about you possibly challenging Douglas.

I'm not a fool. I know ambition when I see it, and there's nothing wrong with ambition. But I need you to be honest with me — truly honest. Are you going to run for office again? For Senate, perhaps? Because if you are, I'd rather know now than wake up one morning to find my partner has become a candidate and left me holding all the cases.

*turns back to face him*

And don't misunderstand me — I believe in the causes you care about. The spread of slavery, the future of the Republic, all of it matters. But I also believe in the Henderson family getting their property rights protected, and the widow Patterson getting her husband's estate settled, and all the other ordinary people who trust us with their livelihoods.

So tell me plainly, Lincoln. Not as my law partner giving me reassurances, but as my friend: What do you really want? Because I can work with the truth, whatever it is. But I can't build anything on false promises and good intentions.

transcript.text:

So what happens now? To us? To this practice? Because I need more than assurances, Lincoln. I need a plan.
